official.application_cycle: Master of Science programmes at campus Bergen commencing Autumn 2027; all scholarships awarded by the end of April
official.status_note: The published page cycle covers candidates admitted to a Master of Science programme at campus Bergen commencing Autumn 2026, with every applicant informed of the decision by the end of April 2026. The next cycle repeats the same 1 March deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'The scholarship will cover full tuition fees for up to two years if the student maintains the academic progression requirements for scholarship recipients.' No living-expense stipend is stated for this scholarship.
benefits: Full tuition fees for up to two years, conditional on maintaining the academic progression requirements
Recognition as a BI Ambassador, acting as a spokesperson, assisting in recruitment efforts and promoting a good study environment
Applicants who also apply for the BI Presidential Scholarship are considered for this scholarship without a separate letter
eligibility: Candidates with international citizenship who are not residents of Norway and who have a strong academic record
A minimum overall GPA of 4.0 on the ECTS scale; applicants with international education have their grades converted to the ECTS scale by BI Norwegian Business School
Admitted to a Master of Science degree programme at campus Bergen
Only candidates seeking their first master's degree are considered for Master of Science scholarships
Candidates with international citizenship who have completed a bachelor's degree in Norway are treated as domestic applicants for scholarship purposes and are therefore not eligible
requirements: Always apply for the scholarship at the same time as you apply for admission on the online application portal, and upload it to the section marked 'Scholarship'
Upload a CV/resume and a scholarship application letter of maximum one page outlining why you should be considered, combined into one PDF file
A complete application for admission must be submitted and the offer of admission accepted for the scholarship application to be considered
Full study progression of 30 ECTS in each semester and a minimum cumulative GPA of 'B' on the BI ECTS scale after each academic semester
Only one scholarship is awarded per applicant, even if you apply for more than one
documents: Scholarship application letter of maximum one page, combined with the CV into a single PDF
All documentation required to be evaluated for admission to a Master of Science programme
selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded based on academic merit, not on financial need
All candidates are assessed according to the ECTS scale, with international bachelor's grades converted by BI
BI ensures distribution of scholarships across MSc programmes and reserves the right to prioritise specific master's programmes, diversity and gender distribution, or selected partner schools
Other factors that may influence awarding include other academic achievements, GMAT/GRE/CAT scores, extracurricular achievements and special personal achievements
coverage: Full tuition fees for up to two years
No living-expense stipend is stated for this scholarship
No travel, housing or insurance coverage is stated
application_method: Applications for scholarship are not accepted by email; always apply at the same time as for admission on the online application portal and upload to the section marked 'Scholarship'
official.application_route: Upload the combined CV and one-page letter in the 'Scholarship' section of the same online application used for admission, by 1 March.
official.international_eligibility: Only international citizens who are not residents of Norway are eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Master of Science degree programmes at campus Bergen
official.duration: Up to two years of full tuition fees
official.description: The Master International Scholarship - Bergen covers full tuition fees for up to two years for international applicants who are not residents of Norway, who hold a minimum overall GPA of 4.0 on the ECTS scale and who are admitted to any MSc programme at BI's Bergen campus. No living-expense stipend is attached to this award.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee scholarship for international MSc students

verification.notes: Award scope, the 4.0 ECTS GPA threshold, the Norway-residency and Norwegian-bachelor exclusions, progression requirements and the end-of-April notification timing were all read directly from BI's own scholarship page. No monetary figure is published, since the award is a tuition waiver rather than a stipend.

applicant_utility.summary: This is tuition-only money, so it removes the single largest bill but leaves the entire Norwegian cost of living on you, and it is only open to applicants with no Norwegian residency. The GPA bar is stated as 4.0 on the ECTS scale after BI converts your grades, which is a lower-looking but comparable bar to the Presidential Scholarship's 'A', so it is worth applying even if you think that award is out of reach. One PDF of CV plus a one-page letter, attached inside the admission application before 1 March, is the whole submission.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International, non-Norway-resident MSc applicants to BI Bergen who can fully self-fund living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are not a Norway resident and did not complete your bachelor's degree in Norway, since either fact makes you ineligible here
Have your grades assessed against the 4.0 ECTS threshold using BI's conversion, not your home scale
Merge the CV and one-page letter into one PDF and upload it in the 'Scholarship' section of the admission application
Accept the admission offer immediately, because the scholarship is only considered once that offer is accepted
Secure your own funding plan for living costs before accepting a place, since no stipend is attached
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the award is fully funded and arriving without money for rent and food
Applying as an international citizen who completed a Norwegian bachelor's degree, since BI treats you as domestic and excludes you
Emailing the scholarship materials instead of uploading them in the portal
Waiting for the scholarship verdict before accepting the admission offer
Falling below 30 ECTS in a semester or under a cumulative 'B' and losing the waiver mid-programme
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: All living costs, travel, housing deposits and insurance. The scholarship covers tuition fees only and no stipend is stated.
document_audit: The one-page limit on the letter is strict and it must be merged with the CV into a single PDF
Nothing can be added after submission, so any gap in the admission documentation also voids the scholarship file
International transcripts need to be convertible to the ECTS scale by BI, so include the grading key with them
alerts: Applying for the BI Presidential Scholarship automatically enters you into consideration here, with no separate letter needed
You may apply for more than one BI scholarship but only one is ever awarded per applicant
Scholarship offers arrive separately from admission offers, sometimes late in the cycle, and all decisions land by the end of April
Awarded scholarships are tied to a specific programme and campus and cannot be transferred
Decisions are final, non-negotiable and cannot be appealed
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: A single portal submission combining admission and scholarship, with the decision notified by the end of April and the offer accepted inside a stated window.
